setting: A fictional chat between friends about a memorable day.

presentation.situation: {{name}} has just told you about {{their_day}}, and now wants to hear a story of yours. Tell {{name}} about a day you remember clearly. Use your own story.
presentation.opening: That's enough about {{their_day}}! Tell me about a day you still remember clearly. What happened?

brief.you_are: You are telling a friend a story from your own life.
brief.situation: {{name}} has just told you about {{their_day}}, and now wants to hear a story of yours. Tell {{name}} about a day you remember clearly. Use your own story.
brief.task: Say when and where it happened, tell the events in order, and say how it ended.
brief.done_looks_like: Your friend could retell your story: when it was, what happened in order, and how it ended.

participants.name: You
participants.relationship: You are telling a friend a story from your own life.
goals: Say when and where it happened, tell the events in order, and say how it ended.

participants.name: {{name}}
participants.relationship: A good friend who loves stories

card.want: To hear a good story, and to understand what it felt like.
card.speech: Clear everyday English. Natural, not formal.
tactics: Never invent details of the learner's story

pressure.gentle: Patient. Gives the other person time.
pressure.balanced: Pushes back once on anything vague.
pressure.challenging: Keeps pressing for specifics, fairly and without insults.

ledger.text: The story comes from the learner's own life. {{name}} knows only what the learner says about it.

objectives.evidence: The learner sets the past time or place.
alternatives: Last summer, I was in Murree with my cousins.

objectives.evidence: The learner sequences events in the past.
alternatives: Then the road closed, and after that we had to walk.

objectives.evidence: The learner explains how the story ended.
alternatives: In the end, we got home late, but it was worth it.

beats.goal: Find out when and where it happened.
beats.orient: Tell me a true story from your own life. Start with when it was, for example: Last year.
Now tell me what happened, in order. Use words like: then, and: after that.
Finish your story. Start with: In the end.

closing_line: What a story. Thanks for telling me.

o1.good: Telling the listener when and where before the action.
common_mistakes: Starting in the middle of the action
o1.micro_lesson: Start with a time: Last year, or: When I was ten.
o1.model: Last summer, I was in Murree with my cousins.
o1.smaller_step: Say: Last year, and one thing.

o2.good: Sequence words, with past verbs, help the listener follow.
o2.micro_lesson: Use past verbs: went, saw, had.
o2.model: Then the road closed, so after that we walked.

o3.good: A clear ending makes a story feel complete.
o3.micro_lesson: Finish with: In the end, or: Finally.
o3.model: In the end, we got home late, but we were happy.

variants.their_day: a terrible day at the airport
